_comment: Feature catalogue. Same variable and same unit on the target (Moon/Mars) side and the Earth side. 'kind': numeric | categorical | ordinal. 'derived': computed by pipeline/compute_scores.py, never typed in by hand.

features.label: Slope
features.tooltip: How steep the ground is, in degrees. 0° is flat.
features.earth_method: Median slope within ~1 km of the site from a 30 m DEM (NASADEM below 60°N, ASTER GDEM above).
features.caveat: Earth DEMs are ~30 m per pixel. SkyFall's limit is defined at 1–5 m scale, so Earth slopes are smoother than the same ground would look at 1–5 m.

features.label: Surface roughness
features.tooltip: How bumpy the ground is: standard deviation of elevation in a small window.
features.earth_method: Standard deviation of elevation in a 3×3 window of the 30 m DEM, median within ~1 km.
features.caveat: Depends on DEM resolution. Only compare values computed at the same pixel size.

features.label: Rock cover (proxy)
features.tooltip: Share of the ground covered by rocks. On Earth this is estimated, not measured directly.
features.earth_method: PROXY: texture of Landsat/ASTER imagery or mapped boulder fields. No global Earth 'rock abundance' dataset was found.
features.caveat: Proxy only. Say so in the presentation.

features.label: Regolith / soil type
features.tooltip: What the loose surface layer is made of (e.g. fine impact dust, volcanic ash, ice-rich mantle).
features.earth_method: From geological maps and literature for each Earth site (team to fill).

features.label: Geology / composition
features.tooltip: Main rock type. Lunar highlands are anorthosite (feldspar-rich); lunar maria and much of Mars are basalt.
features.earth_method: From geological maps and literature for each Earth site (team to fill).

features.label: Temperature swing
features.tooltip: Difference between typical day and night surface temperature.
features.earth_method: MODIS LST day minus night, multi-year mean (or ASTER L2 day/night pairs).
features.caveat: Lunar and Martian swings are far larger than anything on Earth; this feature ranks Earth sites by relative behaviour only.

features.label: Relative cold
features.tooltip: How cold the Earth site is compared with the other Earth candidates (1 = coldest). Used for the Moon because Earth cannot reach PSR temperatures.
features.earth_method: DERIVED by the pipeline: percentile rank of annual minimum land surface temperature (annual_min_lst_K) among Earth candidates.

features.label: Thermal inertia (proxy)
features.tooltip: How slowly the ground heats up and cools down. High values mean firm or rocky ground; low values mean loose dust.
features.earth_method: PROXY: apparent thermal inertia from day/night LST difference, converted to SI units with a thermal model. Must be in the same unit as the Mars value.
features.caveat: Day/night temperature difference alone is NOT thermal inertia. Do not enter raw ΔT here.

features.label: Highest sun angle
features.tooltip: The highest the Sun ever gets above the horizon at this place. Near the lunar south pole it stays only a few degrees up, so shadows are long.
features.earth_method: DERIVED from latitude: 90° − |latitude| + 23.44° (Earth's axial tilt), capped at 90°.

features.label: Ground ice
features.tooltip: 0 = no ice; 1 = seasonal frost only; 2 = permafrost or ice mixed in soil; 3 = massive ice or buried glacier.
features.earth_method: From permafrost/ground-ice maps (external source, verify) and site literature.
features.caveat: Ordinal scale chosen by the team. Moon and Mars evidence is often indirect (UV, neutron, radar).

features.label: Depth to ice
features.tooltip: How far below the surface the ice starts.
features.earth_method: Active-layer thickness or depth to ground ice from permafrost maps or site studies.

features.label: Access & comms
features.tooltip: How practical it is to run a test campaign there (access, permits, safety, communications). 1 = easy.
features.earth_method: Team scoring rubric (see README_DATA.md). Earth-only factor: the target value is always 1.
